## Reconciler Verdict — APPROVE (BINDING)

**Role under adjudication:** critic · **Lens:** Methodology · **Round:** 2
**Claude verdict:** APPROVE · **Codex verdict:** REVISE · **Binding verdict:** APPROVE

### Rationale (condensed from the reconciler's report)

Codex is right on every FACT and on the WORDING, wrong on the REMEDY — and the remedy is what
a REVISE would buy. The nested-untracked residual is real and checkout-dependent, and v3's
strongest sentences overstated what A′ delivers: "makes the flood structurally impossible" is
false as a structural claim (the guarantee is TOP-LEVEL only; the 6,152 KB / 13-file figure is
empirical, this-checkout), and change C clause 3 would have written a false contract into
gotchas.md, since gitignored ≠ rsync-excluded.

Not plan-blocking, for three decisive reasons:

1. **A′ creates no new path class — the residual is include-set-wide and pre-existing.** Every
   existing include tree ships untracked descendants under the same override (`build_rsync_command`
   L1122-1128: excludes are the sole filter; rsync knows nothing of `.gitignore`). A′ widens
   `data/`'s share from 1 to 11 tracked components while structurally eliminating the actual
   measured flood (59 untracked top-level entries, ~43.1 of 43.2 GB). Conventional caches
   (`hf_dl`, `g*_dl`, `store`) are exclude-caught at every depth, covering the three per-issue
   tracked dirs. Applied consistently, Codex's bar condemns the whole include-set design, the
